title: Ammonia (NH₃) — Trigonal Pyramidal
description: Understand the trigonal pyramidal geometry resulting from nitrogen's single lone pair.

steps.prompt: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons. It forms 3 single bonds with H and keeps 1 lone pair. What is the geometry?
steps.explanation: Correct! The single lone pair at the apex of the nitrogen atom pushes the three N-H bonds downward into a pyramidal tent, compressing the angle to 107°.

steps.prompt: Rotate the molecule in 3D by dragging empty space and observe the 3D tripod arrangement of the hydrogen atoms.
steps.explanation: Notice how all three hydrogen atoms lie in one plane while the nitrogen atom sits elevated above them like the tip of a pyramid.

steps.prompt: Why is the bond angle in NH₃ (107°) smaller than in CH₄ (109.5°)?
options: Lone pair – bond pair repulsion is greater than bond pair – bond pair repulsion
steps.explanation: A lone pair spreads out more than a bonding pair, exerting greater repulsion that forces adjacent bonding pairs closer together.
